references.text: The context in which the people spoke against God and Moses, leading the Lord to send snakes as punishment.
Moses reminds the people of their wilderness journey through the great and dreadful desert filled with venomous snakes and scorpions.
Isaiah uses the image of a flying, burning snake (seraph) as a warning against the Philistines.
The prophecy mentions flying, burning snakes in connection with the dangers of the Negev desert.
Paul warns the Corinthians not to test Christ, as some of the Israelites did and were killed by snakes.
God's solution to the snake problem: Moses made a bronze snake that healed those who looked at it.
Jesus refers to the bronze snake lifted up in the wilderness as a foreshadowing of his own crucifixion.
